data.bottom_line: New snow and strong winds are building slabs and drifts that may be sensitive to your weight. Avalanches failing under the newest snowfall, as well as those breaking on weak snow buried deeper in the snowpack, are possible, especially in areas with favored snowfall amounts. Sensitive wind drifts are most likely above 8,000' on slopes that held snow prior to these storms. You can lower your risk of encountering an avalanche by avoiding steep slopes where wind has stiffened the snowpack. Cracking and collapsing of the snowpack are clear indicators that conditions are unstable. We will update this General Avalanche Information on or before Tuesday, December 1st.
